evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: "Plugin UI elements follow the app-level Expert/ELI5 Interaction Mode toggle using tooltip.plugins.* keys, with ELI5 showing only the plugin list and enable/disable toggles while Expert exposes hook details, tool collision config, and timeout settings."

items.impact: The visibility split is normative, but tooltip fallback, focus behavior, screen-reader exposure, localization overflow, and tests proving hidden controls are not operable remain unspecified.
items.statement: ELI5 is limited to the plugin list and enable/disable toggles, while Expert exposes hook, collision, and timeout controls; adversarial GUI and localization states are not fully bounded.
items.title: Expert and ELI5 plugin visibility contract

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: "Catalog-installed plugin, hook, and MCP config bundle lifecycle actions surface whether targets are enabled, loaded, or referenced by Persona settings, distinguish catalog-installed plugins from manual or local ones, and expose reload, deferred apply, or disable-before-remove state when required."

items.impact: Concurrent reload, deferred apply, Persona references, and disable-before-remove can diverge unless precedence, atomicity, and recovery transitions are defined, producing misleading GUI state or unsafe removal.
items.statement: The required lifecycle facets are visible, but the legal transition graph and behavior when only part of a plugin, hook, or MCP bundle reloads or applies are not specified.
items.title: Catalog lifecycle state machine is incomplete

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: "Uninstalling a catalog plugin must not silently delete unrelated local overrides or config-sourced plugins with the same display name."

items.impact: A display-name collision is explicitly unsafe, but without immutable provenance identity, preflight inventory, atomic delete boundaries, and rollback, uninstall can still remove or strand user-owned configuration.
items.statement: Catalog uninstall authority excludes unrelated local overrides and config-sourced plugins, yet the stable ownership key and destructive recovery protocol are not defined.
items.title: Catalog uninstall ownership boundary needs identity

evidence.exact_quote: - "The OpenCode baseline is compatibility reference and does not override Puppet Master deltas."

items.impact: Builders cannot treat JavaScript import, Bun, or built-in override behavior as canonical Puppet Master runtime authority merely because it is preserved for compatibility lineage.
items.statement: The OpenCode plugin model is expressly a compatibility reference subordinate to Puppet Master deltas.
items.title: OpenCode baseline is non-authoritative

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: "Puppet Master uses a platform-agnostic plugin API through WASM modules, subprocess-based entries, or dynamic libraries defined by plugin.json entry, with no JavaScript runtime dependency."

items.impact: WASM, subprocess, and dynamic-library adapters have materially different ABI, crash, isolation, and upgrade behavior; absent common version and lifecycle rules, compatibility and containment are builder-defined.
items.statement: The runtime substrate allowlist and no-JavaScript constraint are explicit, but the shared ABI, version negotiation, adapter isolation, and crash semantics are not.
items.title: Platform-agnostic runtime lacks adapter contract

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: "Puppet Master deltas preserve namespaced aliasing for tool collisions by default, strict priority and lexicographic deterministic load order, typed structured logging, and per-Persona plugin controls as the canonical divergences from the OpenCode baseline."

items.impact: Lexicographic order may differ by case, Unicode normalization, locale, duplicate priorities, or discovery races unless comparison bytes and snapshot timing are fixed.
items.statement: Collision, ordering, logging, and Persona-control deltas are canonical, but deterministic ordering still lacks a falsifiable normalization and concurrent-discovery rule.
items.title: Load-order determinism needs comparison semantics

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: "OpenCode-era experimental.session.compacting subscriptions map to Puppet Master canonical session.compacting at registration time as an alias, with InjectContext versus ReplacePrompt return semantics and first-wins conflict resolution for ReplacePrompt."

items.impact: First-wins can become nondeterministic under concurrent registration, hot reload, mixed alias/canonical subscriptions, or unregister/re-register unless the winner key and lifecycle are specified.
items.statement: Alias normalization and return modes are explicit, while deterministic conflict resolution across registration and reload transitions is not.
items.title: Compaction alias first-wins race

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: "When the claude local binary is used as a CLI-bridged provider, Puppet Master records observed provider-protocol capability evidence for native agents, effort and model selection, fallback models, MCP, plugins, settings injection, and headless JSON or stream-json output; plugin support remains capability-scoped and does not imply every provider account can load Puppet Master plugins."

items.impact: Stale evidence can overstate account capability, while settings-injection evidence may leak sensitive configuration unless provenance, redaction, expiration, and offline behavior are defined.
items.statement: Provider plugin support is correctly capability-scoped, but evidence provenance, freshness, revocation, redaction, and network-loss semantics are absent.
items.title: Provider capability evidence can become stale

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: "Backend acceptance overlay preserves AC-PL01 through AC-PL08 for discovery priority, deterministic load order, hook execution order, tool-execute blocking, central registry routing, built-in collision defaults, typed event logging, and timeout or panic continuation behavior."

items.impact: Named acceptance areas are useful, but repeatable fixtures, expected event fields, timing bounds, and proof that timeout or panic continuation preserves pipeline consistency are not present in this unit.
items.statement: AC-PL01 through AC-PL08 cover the backend behavior families, but the overlay is not independently executable or fully falsifiable from its stated criteria.
items.title: Backend acceptance overlay needs concrete fixtures

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: "Plugins GUI acceptance overlay preserves AC-PL09 requiring the GUI Plugins tab to display all discovered plugins with enable/disable toggles and persist disable state across sessions."

items.impact: A list can falsely appear complete during discovery failure, and persisted disable state can attach to the wrong version or identity; keyboard, screen-reader, overflow, and error presentation have no oracle.
items.statement: The Plugins tab must show every discovered plugin and persist disable state, but incomplete discovery, stale identity, loading, error, accessibility, and localization states are not specified.
items.title: Plugins tab completeness can mislead

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: "Compaction alias acceptance overlay preserves AC-PL10 requiring plugins subscribing to OpenCode-era experimental.session.compacting to be treated as subscribers to canonical session.compacting at registration time, with no runtime distinction."

items.impact: The equivalence rule is clear, but mixed-key duplicate registration, ordering, reload, and unregistration scenarios can violate no-runtime-distinction without dedicated tests.
items.statement: AC-PL10 requires alias equivalence at registration, while adversarial mixed alias/canonical lifecycle cases remain untested by the stated oracle.
items.title: Compaction alias oracle misses mixed registration

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: "Plugin hook blocked outcomes map into explicit blocked-state handling and first-class blocked outcomes when they affect execution, without bypassing scheduler observability, retry classification, recovery-option rendering, queue analysis, or remediation observability."

items.impact: If scheduler state, queue analysis, telemetry, and recovery rendering update non-atomically, operators can see contradictory retry or remediation options and automation can race stale state.
items.statement: Blocked outcomes must propagate through scheduler and remediation surfaces, but emission order, idempotency, and partial-projection recovery are unspecified.
items.title: Hook-blocked propagation lacks atomicity

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: "Plugin-driven execution blocking maps into the canonical runtime blocked model with blocked_reason_code = plugin_hook_blocked, runtime-facing payload exposure of allowed_action_ids[], prerequisite or guard metadata, and preserved_local_work when relevant, without plugin-private retry or recovery semantics."

items.impact: Consumers cannot reliably validate or render recovery if field types, schema version, required guard/prerequisite shape, allowed-action authority, and the condition for preserved_local_work are unresolved.
items.statement: The canonical reason code and recovery-facing fields are named, but their typed schema, required conditions, and producer/consumer ownership are incomplete.
items.title: Plugin-blocked runtime payload is under-typed

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: "Only execution-flow hooks pre_tool_invoke, pre_attempt_start, and pre_node_dispatch may trigger plugin_hook_blocked; observation-only hooks such as post_tool_invoke and post_attempt_complete cannot create plugin_hook_blocked."

items.impact: Observation-only hooks are prevented from changing execution state through plugin_hook_blocked, giving validators a direct negative oracle for unauthorized block attempts.
items.statement: Block authority is explicitly limited to three execution-flow hooks and denied to the named observation-only hooks.
items.title: Plugin blocking hook allowlist is explicit

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: "Plugin-blocked payloads include blocked_reason_code: plugin_hook_blocked, plugin_id, hook_name, block_reason, canonical allowed_action_ids[], and preserved_local_work."

items.impact: Different producers can serialize identifiers, empty action lists, reasons, or preserved work incompatibly, while consumers lack a declared rejection or fallback path for malformed payloads.
items.statement: Required payload field names exist, but types, nullability, cardinality, schema version, malformed-input behavior, and consuming owners are not specified.
items.title: Plugin-blocked metadata lacks a complete schema

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: "Plugins do not invent plugin-private runtime recovery semantics and instead reuse canonical action families and runtime commands."

items.impact: The anti-fragmentation boundary is strong, but no owner or mapping defines which canonical actions apply to each plugin block or what happens when none is authorized or available.
items.statement: Plugin recovery must reuse canonical action families and commands, while selection, authorization, empty-action fallback, and consuming runtime ownership remain external seams.
items.title: Canonical plugin recovery mapping is unresolved

evidence.exact_quote: canonical_text: "PLUG-001 is retired to migration-lineage-only compatibility disposition after Phase 2B batch 211 because Plugins_System-S0068 through S0071 are generated standardization tail material: Owner / Consumer Map, PlanUnits heading, former generated PLUG-001 bridge, and Migration Coverage. Plugins_System-S0001 through S0067 are covered by PLUG-002 through PLUG-062 or explicit structural and split dispositions. PLUG-001 no longer carries source_preserving_planunit compile mode and must not own product coverage."

items.impact: The final disposition is unambiguous, but earlier historical migration paragraphs in the same range still say spans map to PLUG-001; consumers must respect batch chronology and the retired PlanUnit rather than treating every historical statement as current coverage.
items.statement: PLUG-001 is explicitly retired to migration lineage and forbidden from owning product coverage, despite superseded historical mapping prose remaining nearby.
items.title: Retired bridge boundary is clear but chronology-sensitive

evidence.exact_quote: P1-PLUGIN-EXTENSION-POINT-CONTRACTS (P1) is compiled as canonical Puppet Master intent for Typed plugin/UI extension points to avoid monkey patching: Imported external-repo finding extrepo-20260703-0034 / P1-PLUGIN-EXTENSION-POINT-CONTRACTS (P1). The preserved PM gap/delta is: Define typed UI slots and stable context object fields for MCP/tool/session/model/runtime rows; forbid monkey patching privileged surfaces; mutation hooks produce receipts and rechecks. The observed external-repo signal remains source-lineage evidence: Agent Zero added per-row extension points because plugins otherwise used MutationObserver/DOM scanning/store monkey-patching; settings hooks added for credential scanning.

items.impact: Without slot IDs, stable context field types, capability gates, version negotiation, lifecycle, isolation, accessibility obligations, and rejection codes, implementations can remain mutually incompatible or recreate privileged monkey patching under nominal typed APIs.
items.statement: Typed row extension points, privileged-surface protection, mutation receipts, and permission rechecks are required, but the actual typed slot and stable context schemas are not defined here.
items.title: Plugin UI extension-point contract remains abstract

evidence.exact_quote: - Unknown hooks, unsigned privileged packages, and permission/capability mismatches fail install validation before activation.

items.impact: Install-time validation fields do not alone define runtime sandbox enforcement, trust-root rotation or revocation, offline verification, update and downgrade behavior, consent withdrawal, partial install cleanup, or receipt idempotency, leaving critical security lifecycle behavior open.
items.statement: The manifest shape, sandbox profile enum, signature record, hook aliases, and pre-activation rejection cases are concrete, but enforcement and full trust lifecycle semantics are not.
items.title: Manifest validation lacks end-to-end trust lifecycle

segments.summary: Reviewed PLUG-047 through PLUG-053 across GUI mode truth, catalog lifecycle and ownership, compatibility authority, runtime substrates, deterministic deltas, and compaction alias races.
Reviewed provider capability evidence, backend and GUI acceptance overlays, alias equivalence, scheduler-visible blocked propagation, and canonical blocked payload seams.
Reviewed hook blocking authority, payload metadata, canonical recovery scope, retired migration bridge boundaries, and typed plugin UI extension-point intent.
Reviewed the manifest permissions and capabilities schema, sandbox profiles, signature evidence, canonical hook aliases, install rejection behavior, and unresolved trust lifecycle seams.
